names.official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

summary: Most visitors need Myanmar's official tourist eVisa — 28 days, US$50, open to roughly 100 nationalities and valid only for arrival at the main international airports — while ASEAN passport holders enter visa-free for short stays. Ongoing civil conflict keeps most land borders closed to foreigners and large parts of the country off-limits.

payments.text: Myanmar runs on cash. International cards work only at a handful of top hotels, ATMs are unreliable and often empty, and the exchange rate situation is volatile. Bring pristine US dollar notes to change into kyat.

safety.text: Myanmar is in a state of armed conflict following the 2021 military coup — most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel. Fighting, airstrikes and arbitrary detention occur across much of the country, and areas under martial law are closed to foreigners.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cool, dry season — the best weather for Bagan and Mandalay. March to May is extremely hot, and the monsoon runs roughly June to October.

driving.text: Myanmar is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Myanmar yet.

tips.text: Most governments advise against all nonessential travel to Myanmar, and against all travel to large parts of the country. Fighting can erupt with little warning, martial-law areas are off-limits, and consular help on the ground is very limited.

Land crossings with Thailand, China and India are largely closed or barred to foreigners. The eVisa is valid only for arrival at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports. Do not plan an overland entry or exit.
Bring enough pristine, unfolded US dollar bills for your whole trip — torn or marked notes are refused, international cards rarely work, and ATMs cannot be relied on.
Power cuts and internet or mobile-data shutdowns are frequent. Download offline maps, keep some cash and your documents accessible, and note your embassy's contact details on paper.
Shoes and socks come off at every pagoda and monastery, including the long walkways at Shwedagon. Dress with shoulders and knees covered, and step around, never over, seated monks.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Myanmar?
faq.answer: Almost certainly yes. Around 100 nationalities — including the US, UK, EU countries, Australia and most of Asia — can apply for the 28-day tourist eVisa (US$50) at evisa.moip.gov.mm. ASEAN citizens enter visa-free for 14 days (Singapore 30). Everyone else needs an embassy visa.

faq.question: Can I enter Myanmar overland?
faq.answer: In practice, no. The land borders with Thailand, China and India are largely closed to foreign travelers because of the conflict, and the eVisa is valid only at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports — fly in and out.

faq.question: Is Myanmar safe to visit?
faq.answer: Most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel. Armed conflict affects much of the country, including airstrikes and arbitrary detention of foreigners. The main tourist areas see fewer incidents, but the situation shifts quickly. Check your government's advice before booking.

faq.question: How long does the Myanmar eVisa take?
faq.answer: Approval is typically issued within 3 business days. Apply only through the official portal, evisa.moip.gov.mm — third-party sites charge more and add nothing. Print the approval letter to show on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend a Myanmar tourist visa?
faq.answer: The 28-day tourist eVisa is not formally extendable. Short overstays have historically been settled with a per-day fine on departure, but do not rely on this. Plan to leave within your permitted stay.
